# BookMinder — Project Memory

BookMinder is a CLI (heading for MCP) that reads a user's Apple Books library — macOS-only by design — built as a live experiment in whether an LLM can be a good pair programmer under strict outside-in ATDD. It is a deliberately tiny product and a process laboratory: story cards, acceptance specs, and disciplined commits are deliverables alongside the code. The production package (`bookminder/cli.py` → `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`) is small enough to read whole before any task, and the suite under `specs/` is the system's documentation (`pytest --spec`).

This skill is the project's cross-session memory — the environment has none, the repo is the only substrate. Facts here carry their WHY and their verification status; where state can rot, the page points at the command or file that holds truth instead of restating it. It deliberately substitutes for any machine-local memory the environment offers: project knowledge written into a machine-local store cannot reach other machines or cloud sessions, so never store project learnings there. Memory is layered by concern, one source of truth each: this skill holds compiled facts the author has ratified; the product's episodic head is `TODO.md` — read it at load, the order is the plan, with status truth in `stories/` cards; a meta-session's episodic head (coordination, benchmark work) is owned by that session type's own skill and record, and is never mixed into product-development sessions.

Sibling skill `tdd-bdd` carries the process discipline; this skill carries the project.

1 # Apple Books Data Sources 2 3 This document describes the data sources used by Apple Books on macOS and how BookMinder accesses them. 4 5 ## Overview 6 7 Apple Books stores data across multiple files and databases in different container directories. Understanding these data sources is crucial for extracting book metadata, reading progress, and activity information. 8 9 ## Container Directories 10 11 Apple Books uses sandboxed containers to store its data: 12 13 - **com.apple.BKAgentService**: Contains the book files and basic catalog 14 - **com.apple.iBooksX**: Contains databases for reading progress, activity, and UI state 15 16 ## Data Sources 17 18 ### 1. Books.plist 19 20 **Location**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/Books.plist` 21 22 **Purpose**: Primary book catalog with metadata 23 24 **Key Fields**: 25 - `itemName`: Book title 26 - `artistName`: Author name 27 - `path`: Relative path to EPUB file 28 - `updateDate`: Last modification date 29 - `BKPercentComplete`: Only present for **finished books** (always 1.0 = 100%) 30 31 **Important Discovery**: 32 - Contains all books in library (179 total in test case) 33 - Only 22 books have `BKPercentComplete` field (12% of library) 34 - All books with `BKPercentComplete` show 1.0 (100% complete) 35 - Books without this field are either unread or partially read 36 - **Does NOT contain actual reading progress for books in progress** 37 38 ### 2. BKLibrary SQLite Database 39 40 **Location Pattern**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/BKLibrary-*.sqlite` 41 42 **Note**: The filename contains variable numbers (e.g., `BKLibrary-1-091020131601.sqlite`) that change between installations. Use glob pattern matching to locate. 43 44 **Purpose**: Complete library database with reading progress and activity 45 46 **Key Table**: `ZBKLIBRARYASSET` 47 48 **Critical Fields for Reading Progress**: 49 - `ZTITLE`: Book title 50 - `ZAUTHOR`: Author name 51 - `ZASSETID`: Asset identifier (matches Books.plist keys) 52 - `ZREADINGPROGRESS`: Float value (0.0 to 1.0) representing actual reading progress 53 - `ZLASTOPENDATE`: Timestamp when book was last opened (Apple reference date) 54 - `ZISFINISHED`: Integer indicating if book is finished (1 = finished, 0 = not finished) 55 - `ZDATEFINISHED`: Timestamp when book was finished 56 - `ZCREATIONDATE`: When book was added to library 57 58 **Additional Important Fields**: 59 - `ZISSAMPLE`: Integer indicating if book is a sample (1 = sample, 0 = full book) 60 - `ZCONTENTTYPE`: Integer indicating content type (likely: 1 = Book, 3 = PDF) 61 - `ZPATH`: Path to the book file (relative to Books directory) 62 - `ZFILESIZE`: Size of the book file in bytes 63 - `ZSTATE`: Integer indicating download/availability state 64 - `ZGENRE`: Book genre/category 65 - `ZKIND`: Content kind (e.g., "ebook", "pdf") 66 - `ZPAGECOUNT`: Number of pages in the book 67 - `ZISEPHEMERAL`: Integer indicating temporary status 68 69 **Example Query for Recent Books**: 70 ```sql 71 SELECT ZTITLE, ZAUTHOR, ZREADINGPROGRESS, ZLASTOPENDATE, ZISFINISHED 72 FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET 73 WHERE ZREADINGPROGRESS > 0 74 ORDER BY ZLASTOPENDATE DESC 75 LIMIT 10; 76 ``` 77 78 **Sample Results**: 79 - "The Left Hand of Darkness" - Ursula K. Le Guin - 32% progress 80 - "Lao Tzu: Tao Te Ching" - Ursula K. Le Guin - 8% progress 81 - "The Beginning of Infinity" - David Deutsch - 59% progress 82 83 ### 3. Recently Opened Books Database 84 85 **Location**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BCRecentlyOpenedBooksDB/BCRecentlyOpenedBooksDB.sqlite` 86 87 **Note**: This filename appears to be fixed (no variable numbers). 88 89 **Purpose**: Tracks reading sessions and activity 90 91 **Key Table**: `ZBCASSETREADINGSESSION` 92 93 **Fields**: 94 - `ZASSETID`: Asset identifier 95 - `ZTIMEOPENED`: When reading session started (Apple reference date) 96 - `ZTIMECLOSED`: When reading session ended 97 - `ZTIMEUPDATED`: Last update timestamp 98 99 ## Data Relationships 100 101 ### Asset ID Mapping 102 - Books.plist uses keys like "401429854" (numeric strings) 103 - BKLibrary database uses same IDs in `ZASSETID` field 104 - Reading sessions reference same IDs in `ZASSETID` 105 106 ### Progress Data Sources Hierarchy 107 1. **BKLibrary.sqlite** - Authoritative source for reading progress (ZREADINGPROGRESS 0.0-1.0) 108 2. **Books.plist** - Only shows finished books (BKPercentComplete = 1.0) 109 3. **Reading sessions** - Activity timestamps but no progress percentages 110 111 ### Content Type Identification 112 113 **In BKLibrary Database**: 114 - `ZCONTENTTYPE = 1`: Likely regular books (EPUB) - unverified against a live database 115 - `ZCONTENTTYPE = 3`: Likely PDF documents - unverified against a live database 116 - `ZISSAMPLE = 1`: Sample/preview books 117 - `ZKIND = "ebook"`: Standard ebook format 118 - `ZKIND = "pdf"`: PDF document 119 120 **In Books.plist**: 121 - `kind = "ebook"`: EPUB books 122 - `fileExtension = "epub"`: EPUB format 123 - `BKBookType = "epub"`: Book type identifier 124 125 ### Asset ID Correlation System 126 127 Asset IDs provide the link between different data sources: 128 129 **Format**: Numeric strings (e.g., "401429854", "1296850431") 130 131 **Cross-Reference Pattern**: 132 ``` 133 Books.plist key: "401429854" 134 ↓ 135 BKLibrary.ZASSETID: "401429854" 136 ↓ 137 Reading Session.ZASSETID: "401429854" 138 ↓ 139 File path: "401429854.epub" 140 ``` 141 142 **Asset ID Sources**: 143 - iTunes Store ID for purchased books 144 - Generated ID for sideloaded content 145 - Hexadecimal IDs for some system content (e.g., "1F150082C5E6CD9413FAA197989BC910") 146 147 ### Apple Timestamp Format Details 148 149 Apple uses Core Data timestamp format with reference date January 1, 2001, 00:00:00 UTC. 150 151 **Conversion Examples**: 152 ```python 153 # Raw timestamp: 772198715.562895 154 # Converts to: 2025-06-22 20:11:55 UTC 155 156 def apple_to_unix_timestamp(apple_timestamp): 157 # Apple epoch: January 1, 2001 UTC 158 # Unix epoch: January 1, 1970 UTC 159 # Difference: 978307200 seconds (31 years) 160 return apple_timestamp + 978307200 161 162 def apple_timestamp_to_datetime(apple_timestamp): 163 apple_epoch = datetime.datetime(2001, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc) 164 return apple_epoch + datetime.timedelta(seconds=apple_timestamp) 165 ``` 166 167 **Common Timestamp Fields**: 168 - `ZLASTOPENDATE`: When book was last opened 169 - `ZDATEFINISHED`: When book was completed 170 - `ZCREATIONDATE`: When book was added to library 171 - `updateDate` (Books.plist): Last modification (ISO format) 172 173 ### Database Performance and Access 174 175 **File Structure**: 176 - Main database: `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` 177 - Write-Ahead Log: `BKLibrary-*.sqlite-wal` 178 - Shared Memory: `BKLibrary-*.sqlite-shm` 179 180 **Access Pattern**: 181 - Query the main `.sqlite` file 182 - SQLite automatically handles WAL/SHM files 183 - Database may be locked during active Apple Books usage 184 185 **Recommended Query Approach**: 186 ```python 187 import sqlite3 188 import glob 189 190 # Locate database 191 pattern = f"{home}/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/BKLibrary-*.sqlite" 192 db_files = glob.glob(pattern) 193 if not db_files: 194 raise FileNotFoundError("BKLibrary database not found") 195 196 db_path = db_files[0] # Use first match 197 198 # Query with error handling 199 try: 200 with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn: 201 conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row # Enable column access by name 202 cursor = conn.cursor() 203 # Execute queries... 204 except sqlite3.OperationalError as e: 205 if "database is locked" in str(e): 206 # Apple Books is running, retry or prompt user 207 pass 208 ``` 209 210 ### Test Fixtures 211 212 For information on creating and managing test fixtures (including Books.plist, EPUB files, and SQLite databases), see [test_fixtures.md](test_fixtures.md). 213 214 215 ## Apple Books UI Analysis 216 217 ### UI Structure Overview 218 219 Apple Books organizes content in the Home screen with distinct sections that correlate directly to database states: 220 221 1. **Continue Section**: Currently reading books (progress 1-99%) 222 2. **Previous Section**: All previously accessed books (mixed states) 223 3. **Books Read This Year**: Achievement view (finished books only) 224 225 ### Content Types and Indicators 226 227 **Content Types**: 228 - **Book**: Regular ebooks (EPUB format) 229 - **PDF**: Technical documents, manuals, papers 230 - **Sample**: Free previews from the bookstore 231 232 **Status Indicators**: 233 - **Percentage (1%-99%)**: Active reading progress 234 - **"Finished" + blue checkmark**: Completed books (100%) 235 - **"Sample"**: Preview/trial versions 236 - **Cloud icon**: Books stored in iCloud but not downloaded locally 237 238 ### Detailed Section Analysis 239 240 #### Continue Section 241 Shows recently opened books that are either in progress or samples. 7	- **B-40 — Two sandboxed containers (verified@tree, encoded at library.py:17-25).** `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/` holds `Books.plist` (the catalogue) beside per-book `<numeric-id>.epub` items. `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/` holds the library database. 8	- **B-41 — Plist vs database roles (observed-2025; the split is load-bearing for the whole design).** `Books.plist` is a catalogue: `itemName`, `artistName`, `path`, `updateDate`. Its `BKPercentComplete` appears only on finished books (always 1.0) — it cannot express in-progress reading. Real reading state lives in the database table `ZBKLIBRARYASSET` (`ZREADINGPROGRESS`, `ZLASTOPENDATE`, `ZISFINISHED`, `ZDATEFINISHED`, `ZCREATIONDATE`). The database is the authoritative catalogue: titles the database knew were demonstrably missing from the plist even after a fresh `plutil -convert swift` snapshot, and the cause was never established (the author's verdict: still a mystery) — so absence from the plist proves nothing in either direction, neither about library membership nor about cloud status. `updateDate` in the plist is probably publisher-revision metadata rather than reading activity — the author's hypothesis, never verified; what the episode actually settled is that the `sort_by='updated'` feature was deleted as YAGNI precisely because the field's meaning was unknown. BookMinder cares about the user's relationship to the book, which lives in the database. Books lazy-download from iCloud: a book in the catalogue with no file on disk is a valid library entry — never filter books by on-disk file existence.
